To evaluate the generated texts quality, we employed two widely used metrics in ATG: BLEU-4 (B-4) and ROUGE-1 (R-1). These metrics assess the similarity between the generated text and reference based on n-gram overlap. Since paraphrases are commonly used in ad texts, BERTScore (BS), an embedding-based metric, was also used to handle their semantic similarity. Additionally, as task-specific guardrails, we introduce keyword insertion rates (KWD) and sentence length regulation compliance rates (REG).

To clarify the limitations and possibilities of automatic evaluation, we performed a meta-evaluation by adding a GPT-4 based evaluator to the set of the metrics used in the experiment in §5. The GPT-4 based evaluator was constructed by giving the same instructions as those given to the human raters in the manual evaluation §5.2.

guideline: The evaluations were conducted: for faithfulness using absolute evaluation of whether the input document implies the ad text; for fluency using absolute evaluation of understandability and naturalness; and for attractiveness using pairwise comparison with human reference.
annotators assessed ad texts on faithfulness (does the LP imply the ad?), fluency (is it understandable and natural?), and attractiveness (pairwise comparison with human reference).

The main instructions given to the annotators were as follows: 1. Consider the search keyword as the user's intent. 2. Create an advertisement that is consistent with the product/service description in the LP. 3. Ensure that the length of the advertisement is within 15 full-width characters.
